contract.title: Force on a 2D wall-mounted square obstacle in a 40 mm channel at 0.5 m/s
contract.requested_prompt: A 2D square obstacle (side 10 mm) sits on the floor of a channel 40 mm high carrying air at 0.5 m/s. Report the force on the obstacle per unit depth.

objectives.description: Measure the time-averaged streamwise (drag) force per unit depth on the wall-mounted square obstacle (10 mm side) in a 40 mm-high channel with 0.5 m/s uniform air inflow (Re_s = U*s/nu ~ 333 based on obstacle side).

Measure the time-averaged wall-normal (lift) force per unit depth on the same obstacle; a non-zero value is physically expected because the obstacle sits on the floor (no top-bottom symmetry) of the blocked channel.
Verify conservation of mass flux between inlet, outlet and impermeable walls over the simulated unsteady flow, and that the flux monitors remain bounded over the trailing multi-period window.

checks.rationale: For a bluff body at Re~O(300), the drag coefficient referenced to frontal area must be a finite, positive, order-1 quantity; values outside [0,5] indicate a divergent solver or a mis-specified force patch/reference area rather than a physical result.

The wall-normal force coefficient on a wall-mounted obstacle in this low-blockage, laminar regime is expected to be bounded and of comparable magnitude to the drag coefficient; |Cl|>5 would indicate an unphysical or diverging solution.

Direct consistency bound on the reported streamwise force per unit depth, derived from the same [0,5] admissible Cd range scaled by 0.5*rho*U^2*Aref = 0.0015 N/m; catches unit/scaling errors in the derived force independently of the dimensionless coefficient check.

Direct consistency bound on the reported wall-normal force per unit depth, derived from the same [-5,5] admissible Cl range scaled by 0.5*rho*U^2*Aref = 0.0015 N/m; catches unit/scaling errors in the derived force independently of the dimensionless coefficient check.

At Re~300 a 2D square bluff body is expected to shed periodic Karman-type vortices, producing a bounded instantaneous Cd oscillation of roughly 10-50% of its mean (consistent with 2D laminar square-cylinder studies, e.g. Sohankar et al. 1998); a relative span below 1.5 over the trailing multi-period window confirms the solution has reached a bounded periodic (or steady) regime rather than still being transient or numerically diverging. This is a bounded-oscillation/numerical-health criterion, not a claim that the instantaneous force itself is constant.

Incompressible flow carries zero net mass storage at any instant, so the sum of volumetric flux across all boundary patches (inlet+outlet+walls+obstacle) must vanish up to spatial discretization error at every timestep, independent of the flow being unsteady/periodic; 2% is a generous bound given the modest (~12,500-cell) mesh resolution.

The floor/ceiling walls and the obstacle itself are solid no-slip (impermeable) boundaries; any significant net flux measured through them over the run would indicate a leaking boundary condition or a mesh/geometry defect rather than physical flow.

Bounded fluctuation of the inlet/outlet flux monitors over the trailing multi-period window indicates the periodic unsteady solution has reached a repeatable regime; 1.0 (100% relative span) is generous given the outlet flux is itself modulated by vortex shedding, while still catching genuine runaway drift or non-convergence.

assumptions.justification: Stated directly in the request as the channel inflow speed; applied as a uniform velocity profile at the inlet.
Standard atmospheric air properties (~20C, 1 atm) used because the request specifies 'air' without stating temperature/pressure.

Re_s = U*s/nu = 0.5*0.01/1.5e-5 ~= 333 based on the obstacle side length, well within the range where 2D square bluff bodies (confined or not) exhibit unsteady periodic vortex shedding rather than being fully turbulent; no turbulence model is applied and the flow is resolved as transient laminar.

assumptions.value: floor and ceiling both no-slip solid walls
assumptions.justification: 'Channel' denotes a bounded duct; both bounding surfaces are treated as solid no-slip walls, consistent with standard internal-flow terminology.

assumptions.value: upstream fetch 8*s, downstream fetch 21*s, depth 1 m
assumptions.justification: Upstream/downstream fetch chosen generously relative to the obstacle size to let the approach flow and wake develop without strong boundary feedback from the inlet/outlet; the domain is given a 1 m span so the OpenFOAM-reported total force is numerically equal to the force per unit depth.
Graded 5-block structured mesh (~12,480 cells) refined to ~0.42 mm near the obstacle, kept well under the 50,000-cell budget while resolving the obstacle boundary layer and near wake.

limitations: Case is strictly 2D (span-wise infinite obstacle); no 3D end effects are represented.
Flow is laminar (no turbulence model); if the true physical Reynolds number locally exceeds the laminar-to-turbulent transition this would underpredict turbulent mixing in the wake.

Reported force is a time/phase average over a trailing multi-period window of a periodically unsteady signal, not a steady force; the instantaneous force oscillates about this mean due to vortex shedding.
No experimental or literature reference value is claimed for this specific confined (25% blockage) wall-mounted geometry; only internal admissibility/bounded-oscillation checks are used.
contract.reference: No external validation claimed; internal admissibility and bounded-oscillation checks only.
